mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation index followed by a subsequent decline signals the Federal Reserve is pausing rate hikes, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above its 12-month moving average and then falls below it within the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified pause period, or CPIAUCSL does not exhibit the described pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% for two consecutive months predicts wage-price spirals that boost consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 0.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative or flat during the identified labor cost acceleration, or PAYEMS does not meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO manufacturing index coinciding with a drop in RSAFS retail sales signals supply-side weakness, lowering corporate earnings expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 5% in a month and RSAFS falls by more than 3% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the supply shock, or proxies do not meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST housing starts exceeding 1% above the prior month's level for three months indicates strengthening domestic demand, which is associated with higher equity risk appetite and positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 1% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) during the housing expansion, or HOUST does not meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform over the next 20 days due to higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the high-rate period, or FEDFUNDS does not trigger as specified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 3% for three consecutive months suggests labor market softening, reducing wage growth expectations and pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the negative over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3% and remains below for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during the cooling, or UNRATE does not meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 GDP (quarterly) combined with INDPRO falling below 100 (index) signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous quarter and INDPRO < 100 index in the same quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during the contraction, or proxies do not satisfy the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a tightening cycle (indicated by FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling) increases perceived risk premium, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns unless offset by strong corporate earnings news.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rising trend and UNRATE falling trend over 3 months
failure_condition: During the tightening regime, 20-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) when corporate earnings are weak, or proxies do not show the described trend.
